claims.claim: Rio Tinto reported H1 2026 underlying EBITDA of $14.8B, up 28%, free cash flow of $3.8B, up 75%, and 3% copper-equivalent production growth.
Copper, aluminium and lithium contributed more than half of underlying EBITDA, evidence of diversification beyond iron ore.
A September 10 Winu agreement records Nyangumarta consent and a co-designed framework for the proposed copper-gold project.

factors.name: critical-mineral diversification
factors.basis: Primary results show non-iron-ore commodities above half of underlying EBITDA.

factors.name: project social license
factors.basis: Winu project agreement provides concrete consent/governance evidence.

risks.risk: Commodity prices and major-project execution can materially alter cash generation.

unknowns.unknown: Winu remains proposed; final economics and development timing are not established here.

claims.claim: Rio Tinto had banked $870M of productivity benefits by H1 2026 and targeted a $1.8B annualized run-rate by year-end, creating a measurable execution checkpoint.
AP60 commissioning in Quebec began in March 2026 and is expected to complete by year-end with 96 new pots and about 160kt annual incremental primary-aluminium capacity.

factors.name: productivity conversion
factors.basis: Benefits are partly realized rather than solely targeted.

factors.name: capacity ramp
factors.basis: Commissioning is underway but completion remains prospective.

risks.risk: Commissioning schedules and commodity margins can diverge from targets.

unknowns.unknown: Year-end productivity run-rate and full AP60 ramp are future checkpoints.
